successors.name: Portuguese Mozambique
successors.text: 'covered all of Mozambique between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers' (Gaza, Inhambane, Maputo, Sofala and Manica provinces); 'between the Komati (Incomati) and the Zambezi rivers'

capitals.name: Residence on a tributary of the Nkomati River, north of Lourenço Marques (stand-in: Xai-Xai)

ledger.x: 1824: Soshangane founds the Gaza state in southern Mozambique.
1830s: Soshangane subjugates the Tsonga, Chopi and other peoples of the coast between the Komati and the Save.
1837: Soshangane defeats Nxaba and takes the country inland from Sofala.
28 December 1895: Gungunhana is captured at Chaimite and the Gaza lands pass to Portugal.
28 December 1895: the Gaza Empire ends with the capture of Gungunhana at the fortified village of Chaimite; he 'reigned from around 1884 to 28 December 1895'.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Gaza Empire
wars.outcome: The firearms 'were used primarily to combat the Portuguese invasion in 1895' and 'to their greatest extent at the Battle of Magul'; Gungunhana was captured at Chaimite on 28 December 1895 and exiled to the Azores; the Gaza lands were annexed.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; 'Portuguese protectorate (1882-1895)' (infobox) is a status, not a boundary.
